column1: # Buddhist forms that CC-CEDICT does not carry at all.
# A general Chinese dictionary records the modern language. It has 般若 and 南無, because
# those entered ordinary speech, but it has no entry for 迦葉, 舍利弗, 舍衛 or 般涅槃 —
# names that occur tens of thousands of times in the canon and nowhere else. That gap is
# structural, not an oversight, and it is the reason a Buddhist reading dictionary has to
# NOTHING HERE IS INVENTED. Every syllable below is a reading Unihan already attests for
# that character (kHanyuPinyin / kXHC1983 / kTGHZ2013 / kHanyuPinlu); the entry only says
# WHICH attested reading applies to this form. `mix pramana.readings.build` re-checks
# every line against Unihan and refuses to write a file if any syllable is unattested, so
# a typo here fails the build rather than entering the corpus as a fact.

column3: 葉 is attested shè; the conventional reading of Mahākāśyapa's name
舍 is attested shè in transliteration; Śāriputra
闍 is attested shé, not the ordinary dū; Ajātaśatru
般 is attested bō, as in 般若; parinirvāṇa
刹 is attested chà, not the commoner shā; kṣaṇa
